title: I Took the College Printer Quota to the TA Who Printed Flyers

parts.text: I hit a quota wall at 4:56 p.m. on a lab report because the TA had printed two hundred club flyers on the student queue. The lab syllabus said course work first. I was twenty, holding a USB and a dying laptop. The TA said clubs are professional development. I pulled the job history from the printer's web page, which still had the default password on a sticker. Then I emailed the professor the history and the syllabus line. At 5:02 the TA asked who gave me the sticker.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He wants the sticker password while my lab report is still in limbo.

social.video_title: Two hundred flyers ate the student quota — Part 1/2
social.description: Lab report, default sticker, syllabus first. The TA noticed. Would you have waited until Monday?

parts.text: The professor reset quotas and moved club jobs to the department code. I printed at 5:11. The sticker came off. The TA developed professionally on the right account. Default passwords are not a personality. Flyers are not lab reports. I stapled. The queue became a queue. USB went cold in my pocket in a good way.

social.video_title: Club jobs moved to the department code — Part 2/2
social.description: Reset quota, 5:11 print, sticker gone. Was professional development a student page?
